title: WIC (Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children), by state
methodology: Income limits are USDA's WIC Income Eligibility Guidelines for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 (Federal Register, April 29, 2026): 185% of the 2026 HHS poverty guidelines, rounded up to the next dollar, with separate tables for Alaska and Hawaii. State agencies may set lower limits, but not above these or below 100% FPL. State records start from USDA's WIC state agency contact list (fna.usda.gov/wic/apply) and were checked against each state's WIC website on 2026-10-09. A state is listed as offering an online application when its WIC site has an online application, pre-application, interest, referral or appointment-request form to start enrollment (you still complete a WIC appointment). It is listed as not offering one when the state says to apply by phone or in person, and left blank when we could not confirm. Phone numbers come from the state WIC page where it lists one, otherwise from USDA's state agency list. USDA's Food and Nutrition Service web pages now appear under the Food and Nutrition Administration name (fna.usda.gov). Formula contract holders for every state come from USDA FNS's list of current WIC infant formula contracts (page updated July 30, 2026). The contract brand, the name of the benefit card and the approved food list link come from each state's WIC site or documents, checked October 9, 2026, and are left blank where the state's site doesn't name them. On October 16, 2026 we rechecked Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Ohio, Rhode Island, South Dakota and West Virginia on their state WIC sites and filled in the facts we could confirm there.

howToApply.text: Contact a WIC agency where you live to start, by phone or online. The agency schedules an in-person or virtual appointment to finish the application and nutrition check.

incomeLimitFplPct.text: WIC's income limit is 185% of the federal poverty guidelines (the reduced-price school meal standard).

incomeEligibilityGuidelines.note: Gross household income in dollars. For households over 8, add the perAdditionalMember amount for each extra person.

adjunctiveEligibility.text: If you or the children in your care get Medicaid, SNAP or TANF, you may already meet WIC's income rule and do not need to show income under the limit.

unbornChildrenCount.text: If someone in your household is pregnant, you may increase your household size by one for each expected birth.

whoQualifies.text: Women who are pregnant, postpartum (up to 6 months after the end of a pregnancy) or breastfeeding (up to the infant's first birthday), infants, and children up to their fifth birthday. You apply through a WIC agency where you live, and every applicant gets a free health and nutrition check from WIC staff.

whatWicProvides.text: Healthy foods on an eWIC card (fruits and vegetables, baby food, milk, eggs, beans, cheese and more), nutrition education and counseling, breastfeeding support, and referrals to health care and community services, at no cost. Many WIC clinics offer breastfeeding peer counselors, and some WIC clinics provide or rent breast pumps to participants who cannot get one through insurance or Medicaid.

formulaContracts.text: Each state WIC agency awards one infant formula rebate contract to the manufacturer offering the biggest discount, so WIC's standard formula depends on your state. As of July 2026, Abbott (maker of Similac) held the contract in 39 states and DC and Mead Johnson (maker of Enfamil) in 11. If your baby needs a different formula for a medical reason, ask your WIC office.

AK.notes: Applicants fill out printable forms and contact the nearest WIC clinic.

AR.notes: The state WIC page lists the toll-free number as 1-800-235-0002, while USDA's state agency list shows 1-800-253-0002; we show the state office line that both list.

formulaContract.note: California WIC has two contracts: Enfamil for milk-based formulas and Similac for soy.

CO.agencyName: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment
CO.notes: The online form is an appointment request; a WIC staff member follows up.

CT.notes: The online form is an interest form; WIC staff contact you to finish the application.

DC.notes: The phone number is the DC WIC Participant Hub. Online, you can request an appointment.

DE.notes: The Delaware WIC client portal is for scheduling appointments; we could not confirm that new applicants can start an application online.

formulaContract.note: Florida WIC's contract powder formulas are Similac products, including Similac Soy Isomil.

GA.notes: Georgia's WIC page links to Georgia Gateway to apply.

HI.notes: The online link opens Hawaii WIC's pre-application portal. The phone number is from USDA's WIC state agency list; the state WIC page did not show it.

IA.agencyName: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
IA.notes: Iowa says to contact your local WIC office or agency to make an appointment; the phone shown here is from USDA's state agency list.

ID.agencyName: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
ID.notes: Idaho says to contact your local WIC clinic to set up your first appointment. The phone shown here is from USDA's state agency list; for card or PIN problems, Idaho's eWIC customer service line is 844-892-3084.

KS.agencyName: Kansas Department of Health and Environment
KS.notes: The online pre-application starts your enrollment; your local WIC clinic then contacts you. 785-296-3683 is the State WIC office line.

KY.agencyName: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services

LA.notes: The online form is an interest form; your local clinic follows up.

MD.notes: Maryland's WIC page says to call your county WIC office or use the client portal to set up an appointment.

ME.agencyName: Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention
ME.notes: Online, you can use the contact form and a WIC staff member will call to set up an appointment.

MI.agencyName: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
MI.notes: Michigan's WIC page links to MI Bridges to start an application. The phone number is from USDA's WIC state agency list; the state WIC page did not show it.

formulaContract.note: Michigan WIC switches its standard formula from Similac to Enfamil with November 2026 benefits, under a contract that runs November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2031.

MO.agencyName: Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services
MO.notes: The online form is an interest form.

MS.notes: The phone number is the WIC scheduling center. The WIC landing page lists a different toll-free number, (800) 545-6747.

MT.agencyName: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services
MT.notes: Montana's WIC page sends applicants to signupwic.com, a national WIC sign-up site, to start. The phone number is from USDA's WIC state agency list; the state WIC page did not show it.

NC.agencyName: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
NC.notes: Online, you can submit a referral form; a WIC clinic contacts you within 20 days. The phone number is NC's statewide WIC line.

ND.agencyName: North Dakota Health and Human Services
ND.notes: North Dakota says in-person enrollment at a WIC clinic is the only way to apply.

NE.agencyName: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services

NH.agencyName: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
NH.notes: New Hampshire's online pre-application sets up your first appointment. Families moving from another state should call instead.

NJ.notes: New Jersey's online Participant Portal is a 15-minute pre-screening that goes to your local WIC agency, which then schedules your appointment. The state's WIC pages list local agency numbers; the phone shown here is from USDA's state agency list.

NM.notes: Online, you can request an appointment; clinic staff call within 7 days.

NV.agencyName: Nevada Division of Public and Behavioral Health

NY.agencyName: New York State Department of Health

OH.notes: Ohio WIC has a printable application you take to a WIC clinic, not an online form. 1-800-755-GROW (4769) is the state's line for finding your local clinic.

OK.notes: The online form is an interest form.

OR.notes: Some counties use their own interest form, linked from the state page.

PA.notes: The online form is a pre-application sent to your local WIC office.

formulaContract.note: Pennsylvania WIC holds a contract with Abbott Nutrition for standard Similac formulas.

RI.notes: Rhode Island's WIC pages say to call your local WIC office; the phone shown here is from USDA's state agency list. We couldn't confirm an online form to start.

SC.agencyName: South Carolina Department of Public Health
SC.notes: Online, you can complete a pre-application; the phone number makes in-person or online appointments.

SD.notes: The quickest way to start is the WIC Portal; you can also send a request-an-appointment form. South Dakota's WIC site lists county office numbers; the phone shown here is from USDA's state agency list.

formulaContract.note: Tennessee WIC has provided only Similac standard formulas since May 1, 2023.

TX.notes: The online form starts your application; your local WIC office contacts you to set up the first appointment.

formulaContract.note: Texas WIC's milk-based contract runs October 2022 to September 2027 with Mead Johnson; soy formula stays with Abbott.

UT.agencyName: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
UT.notes: Utah says to call or text your local WIC clinic to apply. The phone number is from USDA's WIC state agency list; the state WIC page did not show it.

VA.notes: The phone number is listed on VDH's Contact WIC page.

VT.notes: You can also text Apply to 1-844-839-8942.

WA.notes: The phone number is the WIC Cascades Support Line.

WI.notes: Online, you can complete a pre-application.

WV.agencyName: West Virginia Office of Nutrition Services
WV.notes: The Apply Now button on West Virginia's WIC site starts an online application. 304-558-0030 is the WIC program's general inquiries line.

WY.notes: Online, you can request an appointment. The phone number is from USDA's WIC state agency list; the state WIC page did not show it.
